quality_guards: The need and method for health surveillance depend on the identifiable health effect, residual exposure, valid detection techniques and the work population.
Health-surveillance evidence is exposure-, worker-, hazard- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
Young-worker controls depend on age, maturity, capability, task, equipment, work environment and supervision quality.
Young-worker guidance is person-, task-, equipment- and placement-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Controls depend on pregnancy stage, health advice, work activity, exposure, hours, workplace conditions and individual needs.
Pregnancy and new-mother evidence is person-, stage-, task- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
Diesel-exhaust risk depends on engine type, maintenance, fuel, load, smoke condition, duration, enclosure and ventilation effectiveness.
Diesel-exhaust evidence is engine-, task-, exposure-, location- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level cancer or poisoning probability.
Latex risk depends on protein content, powder, frequency of use, exposure route, sensitisation, task and individual susceptibility.
Latex evidence is product-, exposure-, worker- and sensitisation-specific and is not an exact parcel-level allergy probability.
Lighting effectiveness depends on layout, shadows, glare, weather, vehicle height, maintenance, visual task and transitions between light levels.
Lighting evidence is route-, task-, layout-, visibility- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision or fall probability.
Compressed-air risk depends on pressure, system design, equipment condition, task, exposure profile, decompression procedure and competence.
Compressed-air evidence is system-, task-, pressure-, worker- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Cleaning and catering risk depends on product chemistry, dilution, incompatibilities, task, contact time, ventilation, hygiene and PPE selection.
Cleaning and catering evidence is chemical-, task-, worker-, ventilation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
BESS risk depends on battery chemistry, state of charge, capacity, enclosure, thermal management, electrical design, location and emergency response.
BESS evidence is technology-, installation-, operating-, location- and incident-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.
Sun and outdoor-work risk depends on UV intensity, season, duration, skin type, clothing, shade, workload, heat and hydration.
Sun-exposure evidence is person-, weather-, task-, season- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level skin-cancer probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
